summary: This educational survival game immerses players in the harsh, scientifically accurate environment of Mars, blending interactive STEM learning with thrilling resource management. Stranded on the Red Planet, players must apply real physics, chemistry, and engineering principles to stay alive. Core gameplay mechanics involve extracting subsurface water ice, generating breathable oxygen through electrolysis, cultivating hydroponic crops, and maintaining solar power grids against relentless Martian dust storms. By solving realistic scientific challenges, players construct and expand a sustainable base habitat while exploring iconic geological landmarks like Olympus Mons and Valles Marineris. Designed specifically for students and curious science enthusiasts, the game transforms complex aerospace concepts and planetary science into engaging, hands-on problem-solving missions. Ultimately, this interactive adventure fosters critical thinking, strategic resilience, and deep curiosity about space exploration, empowering players to master the essential science required for humanity’s future on Mars.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

This project is an interactive 3D educational survival game set on the surface of Mars. Stranded on the Red Planet, players must manage vital survival resources—oxygen, water, power, and food—by applying real-world STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) principles. Gameplay revolves around scientifically grounded mechanics: mining subsurface water ice, running electrolysis systems to generate breathable oxygen, maintaining hydroponic greenhouses, and protecting solar arrays from dynamic Martian dust storms. Players progress by solving realistic physics, chemistry, and engineering puzzles to upgrade their base and explore authentic Martian landmarks such as Olympus Mons and Valles Marineris.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Experiential STEM Learning: Transforms abstract textbook theories in thermodynamics, chemistry, and orbital mechanics into tangible, hands-on problem-solving challenges.
  • Critical Thinking & Resilience: Encourages players to analyze cause-and-effect relationships, manage scarcity under pressure, and iterate on failed designs without real-world risk.
  • Inspiring Future Explorers: Aims to spark curiosity in aerospace, planetary science, and sustainability among students and science enthusiasts, demonstrating the real scientific hurdles humanity must overcome to become a multi-planetary species.

Tools, Technologies & Hardware Used

  • Game Engine & Software: Unity (or Unreal Engine) for 3D environment rendering, physics simulation, and gameplay systems; Blender for 3D modeling of rovers, habitats, and Martian terrain; Figma/Photoshop for UI/UX and HUD design.
  • AI & Development Assistants: Claude (Anthropic) was utilized throughout the development lifecycle to assist with code generation, debugging complex C#/Python scripts, designing scientific mission scenarios, and structuring in-game educational dialogues.
  • Programming Languages: C# (for Unity scripting, resource logic, and AI systems) / C++ and Blueprints (if using Unreal Engine), alongside Python for data balancing and simulation modeling.
  • Scientific Data & APIs: NASA open-source Martian elevation maps (MOLA) and atmospheric datasets to ensure realistic terrain topology, gravity ($3.721\text{ m/s}^2$), and day/night cycles.
  • Hardware: Standard development workstations (PC/Laptop) with dedicated GPUs for 3D rendering, tested across standard desktop setups (keyboard/mouse) and optional controller support for classroom accessibility.

Creativity & Innovation

Rather than relying on passive quizzes or sci-fi fantasy tropes, the game embeds educational content directly into core survival mechanics—meaning science is the primary survival tool. If a player miscalculates solar panel angles or fails to balance chemical inputs for oxygen generation, the habitat reacts dynamically. Combining high-stakes survival tension with authentic NASA-inspired planetary data and AI-assisted narrative design creates an engaging "stealth-learning" experience where players master complex concepts organically through play.

Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Scientific Accuracy vs. Fun: Balancing realistic planetary constraints (such as Martian atmospheric pressure, radiation, and low temperatures) with intuitive, enjoyable pacing so the game remains challenging rather than frustrating.
  • Accessibility & Cognitive Load: Designing clean, intuitive interfaces and progressive tutorials so players without a strong science background can grasp complex concepts step by step.
  • Performance Optimization: Ensuring smooth frame rates on mid-range school and home computers so educational institutions can run the software without requiring high-end gaming hardware.
  • Curriculum Alignment: Structuring in-game missions and milestones to align with middle and high school physics, chemistry, and earth science standards.
